full_name: Centre for the Study of Existential Risk
mission: CSER is a Cambridge University research centre co-founded in 2012 by Lord Martin Rees, Huw Price and Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn. It studies risks that could cause global catastrophe or human extinction — from AI and biotechnology to climate and systemic collapse — and works with policymakers to reduce them. It also trains new researchers through a PhD and MPhil in Global Risk and Resilience.

key_work.title: Risks from Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technologies (research theme)
key_work.plain_summary: CSER's AI programme: work on near- and long-term AI risks, AI governance and how to steer AI development in safe and beneficial directions.

key_work.title: The Malicious Use of Artificial Intelligence: Forecasting, Prevention, and Mitigation
key_work.plain_summary: A landmark multi-institution report (CSER, FHI, OpenAI and others) on how AI could be misused for hacking, disinformation and physical attacks, with recommendations to prevent it.

key_work.title: Toward Trustworthy AI Development: Mechanisms for Supporting Verifiable Claims
key_work.plain_summary: Proposes concrete tools — audits, red-teaming, bounties, hardware and software checks — so AI developers' safety claims can be verified by outsiders.

key_work.title: Managing Extreme Technological Risks (research project)
key_work.plain_summary: Cross-cutting work on how institutions can foresee and manage low-probability, extreme-impact risks from new technologies.

key_work.title: A Science of Global Risk (research project)
key_work.plain_summary: Builds methods for studying global catastrophic risk rigorously, even when evidence is scarce.

status_note: part of the University of Cambridge's Institute for Technology and Humanity (ITH) since 2023
status_raw: active — part of the University of Cambridge's Institute for Technology and Humanity (ITH) since 2023
size_note: Grew to a full-time team of fourteen after its first researchers started in 2015 (CSER 'Our story')

warnings.text: For the first time, one species — us — holds the future of the planet in its hands.
Advanced AI could cause catastrophic harm through misuse or loss of control if not developed in safe directions.
AI can be misused for cyberattacks, disinformation and physical attacks.
Global risks interact: pushing past environmental tipping points or pandemics can cascade into wider collapse.

recommendations.text: Make AI developers' safety claims verifiable through audits, red-teaming and incident sharing.
Engage policymakers early on extreme technological risk.
Build an interdisciplinary global research field and train new researchers in global risk.
